evidence.excerpt: Igor Starčević received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and his Ph.D. in Technical Sciences from the same institution in 2018, with a dissertation on regression-based fault indicators for photovoltaic SCADA telemetry. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as a teaching assistant in 2013 and was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019. His group focuses on time-series anomaly detection, predictive maintenance pipelines, and performance degradation modelling for distributed energy assets including solar parks, small wind installations, and district heating substations. He teaches courses in machine learning and industrial data systems. The group regularly works with real SCADA datasets and uses a GPU-equipped workstation cluster and the university's HIL (hardware-in-the-loop) test bench for validation experiments.
